more.def: A sudden, strong rush or increase of something, such as water, electricity or a feeling.
examples: A surge of water rushed down the river after the heavy rain.
She felt a surge of pride when she crossed the finish line.
A power surge made the lights flicker.

easy.def: A doctor who fixes the body by operating.
examples: The surgeon fixed his arm.
A surgeon works in the hospital.
The surgeon wore a mask.

more.def: A doctor who does operations to fix people's bodies.
examples: The surgeon fixed the broken bone.
A surgeon washes her hands before an operation.
My uncle is a surgeon at the hospital.

easy.def: When doctors fix your body by cutting.
examples: He had surgery on his knee.
Grandma needs surgery.
The surgery was a success.

more.def: A medical treatment in which a doctor cuts into the body to fix a problem.
examples: She had surgery on her arm.
The doctor explained the surgery to the family.
Surgery can fix broken bones.

easy.def: Having to do with surgery.
examples: The surgeon wore a surgical mask.
The surgical tools are clean.
A surgical team worked.

more.def: Having to do with operations that doctors perform on the body.
examples: Surgical gloves keep germs away from the patient.
The surgical tools were kept clean.
A surgical team prepared for the operation.

easy.def: Rude and in a bad mood.
examples: The man was surly.
A surly look.
The surly guard grunted.

more.def: Rude, bad-tempered and unfriendly.
examples: The surly guard grunted and waved us on.
He gave a surly answer.
The surly cat hissed at everyone.

easy.def: To guess from clues.
examples: I surmised he was tired.
She surmised it would rain.
He surmised who it was.

more.def: To guess that something is true from the clues you have.
examples: I surmised that he was tired when he yawned.
She surmised from the dark clouds that it would rain.
He surmised the answer.

easy.def: To get over a difficulty.
examples: She surmounted the problem.
He surmounted the wall.
They surmounted the hill.

more.def: To overcome a difficulty or to climb over something.
examples: She surmounted her fear of heights.
The climbers surmounted the steep ridge.
He surmounted the wall with a ladder.

easy.def: Your family name.
examples: My surname is Smith.
What is your surname?
Her surname is long.

more.def: The name that all the people in a family share, said after the first name.
examples: Write your first name and your surname on the paper.
Her surname is the same as her father's.
In many places, the surname comes at the end of a name.

easy.def: To do better than.
examples: She surpassed her best time.
He surpassed his sister.
The tower surpasses the hill.

more.def: To be better than, or to go beyond a limit.
examples: She surpassed her own record in the race.
The tower surpasses all the other buildings in height.
The team surpassed the goal for the food drive.

easy.def: More than what is needed.
examples: We had a surplus of apples.
The farm had a surplus.
A surplus of food.

more.def: An amount that is more than is needed.
examples: We had a surplus of apples after the harvest.
The farm sold its surplus of corn.
A surplus of rain flooded the field.

easy.def: Something you did not know would happen.
examples: The party was a surprise!
I have a surprise for you!
What a nice surprise to see you!

more.def: Something that happens that you did not expect.
examples: It was a nice surprise to find a letter in the mailbox.
To my surprise, the cat liked the bath.
The ending of the book was a complete surprise.

easy.def: Feeling that something happened that you did not expect.
examples: I was surprised by the gift.
She looked surprised.
He was surprised to see snow.

more.def: Feeling or showing that something unexpected has happened.
examples: I was surprised to see my cousin at the door.
She looked surprised when the lights came on.
We were surprised by the sudden storm.

easy.def: Not what you expected.
examples: The news was surprising.
A surprising gift.
It was a surprising ending.

more.def: Causing a feeling of surprise because it was not expected.
examples: It was surprising how quickly the snow melted.
We got a surprising gift in the mail.
The movie had a surprising ending.

easy.def: In a way that is not expected.
examples: The test was surprisingly easy.
It was surprisingly cold.
She was surprisingly fast.

more.def: In a way that is a surprise.
examples: The old car ran surprisingly well.
It was surprisingly cold in the cave.
The little dog was surprisingly fast.

easy.def: Strange, like a dream.
examples: The scene was surreal.
A surreal painting.
It felt surreal.

more.def: Strange and dreamlike, as if not real.
examples: The painting showed a surreal scene of melting clocks.
It felt surreal to stand on the moon in a game.
The foggy morning felt surreal.

easy.def: A kind of art that looks like a strange dream.
examples: Surrealism is odd art.
Surrealism is a style of art.
Surrealism looks like a dream.

more.def: A style of art and writing that shows strange, dreamlike pictures and ideas.
examples: The melting clocks are famous surrealism.
Surrealism looks like a dream.
She likes the strange pictures of surrealism.

easy.def: To give up.
examples: The team would not surrender.
He surrendered the toy.
The king surrendered.

more.def: To give up and stop trying to win or resist.
examples: The chess player had to surrender when the game was lost.
The king surrendered his crown.
She surrendered the toy to her brother.

easy.def: A small carriage pulled by a horse.
examples: A surrey has wheels.
The horse pulled the surrey.
We rode in a surrey.

more.def: A light carriage with four wheels, pulled by a horse, with two seats.
examples: The horse pulled the surrey down the lane.
A surrey has two seats and a fringe on top.
We took a ride in a surrey at the fair.

easy.def: To be all around something.
examples: A fence surrounds the yard.
Water surrounds the island.
Trees surround the house.

more.def: To be on all sides of something.
examples: A moat surrounded the castle.
Water surrounds the little island.
Mountains surround the valley.

easy.def: The things and places around you.
examples: I like my surroundings.
The surroundings were quiet.
Look at your surroundings.

more.def: The things, places and conditions that are all around a person or a thing.
examples: The cabin's surroundings are full of trees and birds.
The chameleon changes color to match its surroundings.
She felt calm in the quiet surroundings of the library.

easy.def: A set of questions to find out what people think.
examples: We took a survey.
The survey asked about pets.
The survey is short.

more.def: A set of questions that is asked of many people to find out what they think.
examples: We took a survey about favorite pets.
The survey showed that most students like pizza.
The survey had five questions.

easy.def: To look carefully over an area.
examples: He surveyed the field.
She surveyed the room.
They surveyed the land.

more.def: To look over or measure something carefully.
examples: He surveyed the field from the hill.
She surveyed the room before leaving.
Workers surveyed the land for the new road.

easy.def: A person who measures land.
examples: The surveyor measured the land.
A surveyor uses a tool.
The surveyor drew a map.

more.def: A person whose job is to measure land and make maps of it.
examples: The surveyor measured the field with a long tape.
A surveyor marks the edges of the land.
The surveyor drew a plan of the park.

easy.def: Staying alive.
examples: The animals' survival depends on water.
Survival is hard in the desert.
The survival of the plant is certain.

more.def: The state of staying alive in hard conditions.
examples: Scientists study the survival of whales in cold seas.
Survival in the desert is hard.
The hikers learned survival skills.

easy.def: To stay alive.
examples: Plants need water to survive.
Fish can not survive out of water.
The plant survived the cold.

more.def: To stay alive, especially through something hard or dangerous.
examples: Camels can survive for days without drinking water.
The sailors survived the storm.
Few plants can survive in such dry soil.

easy.def: A person who stays alive after something terrible.
examples: The survivor was rescued.
The survivors were safe.
He is a survivor of the flood.

more.def: A person who lives through a dangerous event.
examples: The survivors of the shipwreck were rescued.
The lone survivor was found clinging to a log.
The survivors were wrapped in warm blankets.

easy.def: Likely to be harmed by something.
examples: Plants are susceptible to frost.
I am susceptible to colds.
Babies are susceptible to germs.

more.def: Easily affected by something, especially something harmful.
examples: Young plants are susceptible to frost.
Some people are susceptible to colds in winter.
The old paint was susceptible to damage from rain.

easy.def: A Japanese food of rice and fish rolled up.
examples: We ate sushi.
Sushi is made with rice.
I like sushi.

more.def: A Japanese food made of cooked rice rolled with fish, egg or vegetables.
examples: We ate sushi at the restaurant.
The chef rolled rice and cucumber to make sushi.
Sushi is often eaten with chopsticks.

easy.def: A person who may have done something wrong.
examples: The police questioned the suspect.
The detective found a suspect.
The suspect ran away.

more.def: A person who is thought to have done a crime.
examples: The detective questioned the suspect.
The police looked for the suspect.
No suspect has been found.

easy.def: To think something is true without being sure.
examples: I suspect it will rain.
She suspects her brother ate it.
He suspected a trick.

more.def: To think that something is probably true, or that someone did something, without being sure.
examples: I suspect the cat ate the fish.
She suspected a surprise party.
He suspected the story was a joke.

easy.def: To hang something from above.
examples: The lamp is suspended from the ceiling.
A rope suspends the swing.
They suspended the sign.

more.def: To hang something so that it does not touch the ground, or to stop something for a while.
examples: The lamp was suspended from the ceiling.
The bridge is suspended by thick cables.
The game was suspended because of rain.

easy.def: Straps that hold up your pants.
examples: He wore suspenders.
The suspenders are red.
My suspenders hold up my pants.

more.def: A pair of straps worn over the shoulders to hold up pants.
examples: Grandpa wore red suspenders to hold up his pants.
The suspenders stretched over his shoulders.
He clipped his suspenders to his trousers.

easy.def: The exciting feeling of waiting to find out what happens.
examples: The story was full of suspense.
I waited in suspense.
The suspense was too much.

more.def: The exciting or nervous feeling you get while you wait to find out what will happen next.
examples: The story was full of suspense, and I could not stop reading.
We waited in suspense as the judges announced the winner.
The music added suspense to the scene in the movie.

easy.def: When something is stopped for a while.
examples: There was a suspension of the game.
A suspension of the mail happened.
The suspension lasted two days.

more.def: A short stop in something, or being kept from school or a team for a time as a punishment.
examples: The suspension of the game lasted ten minutes because of rain.
He was given a two-day suspension from the team for breaking a rule.
A suspension of bus service left many people waiting.

easy.def: The parts on a car that make the ride smooth.
examples: The truck has a good suspension.
A suspension helps on bumpy roads.
The suspension was fixed.

more.def: The springs and other parts of a vehicle that make the ride smoother over bumps.
examples: The truck's strong suspension made the bumpy road feel smooth.
A mountain bike has a suspension to soak up bumps on the trail.
The mechanic repaired the suspension of the old car.

easy.def: A feeling that something is wrong.
examples: I had a suspicion.
The suspicion grew.
She has a suspicion.

more.def: A feeling that something is not right, even if you have no proof.
examples: I had a suspicion that someone ate the cookies.
His suspicion grew when he heard a noise.
She looked at the stranger with suspicion.

easy.def: Feeling that something is wrong.
examples: The dog was suspicious of the stranger.
I felt suspicious.
The noise was suspicious.

more.def: Feeling that something is not right, or making you feel that way.
examples: The cat was suspicious of the new toy.
I felt suspicious when the lights went off.
The suspicious noise made us check the door.

easy.def: To keep something going.
examples: Food sustains us.
Rain sustains the plants.
He sustained his effort.

more.def: To keep something alive or going over time.
examples: Food sustains us through the day.
Rain sustains the plants during the summer.
He sustained his effort until the race was over.

easy.def: Able to last without using up what we need.
examples: Solar power is sustainable.
A sustainable farm.
Sustainable fishing.

more.def: Able to continue without using up resources or harming the environment.
examples: Wind power is a sustainable way to make electricity.
They practice sustainable farming.
Sustainable fishing leaves enough fish for the future.

easy.def: Food that keeps you alive.
examples: The bread gave them sustenance.
They needed sustenance.
Water is sustenance.

more.def: Food and drink that give you the energy to live.
examples: The hikers needed sustenance after the long climb.
Bread and water gave them sustenance.
The nuts provided sustenance for the squirrels.
